name: Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukemia in Children Without Down Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Blasts show megakaryocytic differentiation confirmed by immunophenotyping (CD41, CD61, or CD42b positivity)
No clinical or genetic evidence of Down syndrome
Presence of characteristic cytogenetic abnormalities such as t(1;22)(p13;q13) in infants

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% blasts in marrow or blood with megakaryocytic immunophenotype and absence of Down syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Immunophenotyping and cytogenetics are essential for accurate diagnosis and subclassification.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe low platelet counts leading to petechiae and mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: very low platelets with bleeding risk
bleeding tendency due to low platelets
marrow infiltration by immature platelet cells
pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to leukemic infiltration

common.symptomName: Fever due to infection or leukemic process

occasional.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement symptoms (headache, cranial nerve palsies)
searchTerms: headache and nerve palsies from brain involvement
central nervous system symptoms including headache
breathing problems from leukemic cell infiltration
lung symptoms caused by cancer cells
small red or purple skin spots

rare.notes: Rare solid tumor masses of leukemic cells

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to leukemic infiltration
searchTerms: renal impairment due to cancer infiltration

rare.symptomName: Cardiac tamponade secondary to leukemic infiltration
searchTerms: cardiac tamponade due to cancer cells

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing circulating megakaryoblasts
Immunophenotyping positive for CD41, CD61, CD42b
Thrombocytopenia, anemia, and variable leukocyte counts
imaging: MRI or CT for CNS involvement if neurological symptoms present

distinguishingFeatures: Different immunophenotype (CD13, CD33 positive, CD41 negative)
Lymphoid lineage blasts positive for CD19, CD10
Occurs exclusively in children with Down syndrome

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe thrombocytopenia with bleeding
Presence of >20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
references: Arber DA, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, Revised 4th Edition, 2016.
Pui CH, et al. Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia in children without Down syndrome: clinical features and outcomes. Blood. 2011.
Orphanet: Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia in children without Down syndrome (ORPHA:329469).
